requirement: EPIC-1 · Story 1.1 — Beat replica shell: a static, stealth-styled, interactive on-screen replica of the Stylophone Beat. Circular SVG pad with native numbering (1,1.5,2,2.5,3,4,4.5,5,5.5,6,6.5,7), a rotary tempo knob whose angle reflects BPM, a speaker-grille info display showing the BPM number, CLICK/PLAY/REC transport buttons, and MODE (DRUMS/BASS) + sound-bank (ROK / others disabled) switches. No sound yet (that is 1.2) but pad click handlers are wired. This is the first UI story; it also does the one-time Vite + React + TS frontend scaffold.

architecture.decision: No open fork — the stack and design are fully locked in README.md and EPIC-1-instrument.md (React + TS + Vite, Tone.js owns timing, SVG circular pad, stealth theme, Anthropic-orange accent, brightness=state). Recorded here as fixed constraints, not re-decided.
seams: App-level local state (no persistence in 1.1): bpm:number (default 120, range ~40-240), mode:'drums'|'bass' (cosmetic in v1, ROK-only), selectedSound:'ROK'. Lifted into App.tsx; child components receive value + change callbacks.
Pad geometry fixed: 12 pitch positions in native numbering 1,1.5,2,2.5,3,4,4.5,5,5.5,6,6.5,7 (no 3.5, no 7.5). padId is the numbering STRING, e.g. '1.5'. onPad(padId:string) fires on wedge tap.

Tone.js is the locked timing owner for later stories (1.2+). Story 1.1 wires NO audio/transport — knob just updates a number, PLAY/REC are styled buttons with handlers stubbed. Never introduce setInterval.
Stealth theme via CSS custom properties: matte charcoal bg, grey surfaces, soft-white text, single accent = Anthropic orange (#D97757-ish), brightness encodes state. Grille = BPM info display.
Component split: App.tsx (state + two-pane layout), BeatPad.tsx (SVG pad), TempoKnob.tsx (rotary + grille BPM), TransportControls.tsx (CLICK/PLAY/REC + MODE + bank switches).
Two-pane CSS-grid layout placeholder now (replica left, structure pane right); FULL responsive + a11y baseline is story 1.6 — do not build it here, just don't block it (semantic controls, focusable).

tasks.title: BeatPad SVG component — 12 wedges, native numbering, click handler
tasks.intent: Build src/BeatPad.tsx: an SVG circular pad with 12 pitch-position wedges labelled in native numbering 1,1.5,2,2.5,3,4,4.5,5,5.5,6,6.5,7 arranged around the circle. Each wedge is a hit region; clicking/tapping (or Enter/Space when focused) fires props.onPad(padId) with the numbering STRING. Stealth-styled wedges with the orange accent on active/hover. Mount it in App's left pane, wired to a handler that logs/records the pad id.
tasks.constraints: Exactly 12 wedges in the locked order/numbering (no 3.5, no 7.5). padId = the numbering string (e.g. '1.5'). SVG geometry (precise wedges + labels). Each wedge focusable and keyboard-activatable (role=button / tabindex) — a11y baseline is native here, full a11y is story 1.6. Use the theme CSS variables, do not hardcode colors. No audio (that is 1.2). ponytail-comment any geometry shortcut.
tasks.acceptance: Pad renders 12 correctly-labelled wedges in the stealth theme; clicking a wedge fires onPad with the correct id (verify '1.5' etc.); each wedge is keyboard-focusable and activates on Enter/Space.
tasks.visual: Circular 12-wedge pad renders with correct native-numbering labels; clicking a wedge shows the fired padId (e.g. via an on-screen readout or console).
tasks.result: src/BeatPad.tsx = SVG donut, 12 <path> wedges mapped over PAD_IDS (30 deg each, clockwise from 12 o'clock), each a role=button tabIndex=0 aria-label 'Pad N' firing onPad(padId) on click + Enter/Space (Space preventDefault). src/BeatPad.css uses theme vars only (idle --surface; hover/focus --accent + glow; active --accent-bright). Mounted in App via <BeatPad onPad={handlePad}/>. Verified in browser: 12 wedges labelled 1,1.5,2,2.5,3,4,4.5,5,5.5,6,6.5,7 in order; clicking 1.5 wedge lit orange + readout 'PAD: 1.5'. Build clean.

tasks.title: TempoKnob rotary + grille BPM display bound to bpm state
tasks.intent: Build src/TempoKnob.tsx: a rotary knob control whose visual angle reflects the current bpm, draggable (pointer) and adjustable by keyboard arrows, calling props.onBpmChange within a clamped range (~40-240). Build the speaker-grille info display that shows the current BPM number. Wire both to App's bpm state so turning the knob updates the grille number live.
tasks.constraints: Knob angle maps to bpm; clamp to the range. Keyboard: ArrowUp/Down (and Left/Right) nudge bpm; control is focusable. Grille shows the number only (BPM). No Tone.js/transport wiring yet (1.3 owns transport) — knob only updates the number. Theme CSS variables. ponytail: no external knob/gauge library, hand-roll the rotary with SVG/CSS transform.
tasks.acceptance: Knob turns (pointer drag + arrow keys) and the grille BPM number updates live and stays clamped to range; knob is keyboard-focusable.
tasks.visual: Rotary knob visibly rotates as BPM changes; grille shows the matching BPM number; dragging/arrow keys update both.
tasks.result: src/TempoKnob.tsx = hand-rolled rotary (CSS transform:rotate, linear bpm->angle over 270deg arc [40,240]->[-135,+135], glowing pointer) + speaker-grille panel (repeating-linear-gradient) showing large live BPM digits. Pointer drag via setPointerCapture (up=faster, 2px~1bpm); role=slider tabIndex=0 aria-valuenow/min/max, ArrowUp/Right +1, ArrowDown/Left -1, PageUp/Down +/-10, clamped+rounded to [40,240]. Mounted <TempoKnob bpm onBpmChange={setBpm}/>. Verified in browser: focus ring appears, ArrowUp x15 moved 120->135 with pointer rotation + grille + readout all live. Build clean. (Note: browser key name must be 'ArrowUp' not 'Up'.)
